chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: The Lil Armstrong recording date
summary: Allen asks about the Columbia sides with Lil Armstrong, Ory, St. Cyr and Johnny Dodds; Mitchell barely remembers the single date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask a little bit about those records you made with Lil Armstrong. You and St. Cyr and Ori and Johnny Dodds was on the date. Yes, yes. Those, that's right. I... Papa Dip. Uh-huh. And let's see, Perdido Street Blues and Gate Mouth. Yeah. There were quite a few of those. Yes, yes, yes. Yeah, that was Lil's outfit. Were you working with her at the time? At the Dreamland? Let's see. No, let's see what...I don't know.
I don't think I was with her then. I can't remember where...no.
Yeah. But I don't think I was at the Dreamland with her then. Uh-huh. I don't know. I can't remember where that was before I was there with the Dreamland or after.
It was about 1926, I believe, when the records were made. Were made, yeah. Yeah. They say Armstrong was in New York with Henderson. Yeah, he left there for...yeah.
When I was over...over at Dreamland there, he left with...Iain Buster Bailey. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Well that must have been... Do you remember anything about those dates? I think that was Ori and St. Cyr and Dodds, some of the best records they made, and you sound wonderful on those too. Yeah.
Let's see, and you know, I almost forget about Lil making recordings with Lil. I do remember that now. Yeah, I think it was one date.
Those are some good records, alright.
